stimuli.title: Case study: heart failure exacerbation
stimuli.text:
Emergency department, 1400. A 72-year-old client with heart failure (ejection fraction 30%), hypertension and type 2 diabetes comes in with 4 days of worsening shortness of breath. The client says, "I have to sleep sitting up in my recliner now." The client ran out of furosemide 1 week ago and ate ham and canned soup at a family gathering over the weekend.

Home medications: furosemide 40 mg PO daily, lisinopril 10 mg PO daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily, metformin 500 mg PO twice daily.

| Assessment | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 158/94 mm Hg |
| Heart rate | 108/min, regular |
| Respirations | 28/min |
| SpO2 | 89% on room air |
| Temperature | 98.4 F |
| Weight | 84.5 kg (clinic weight 2 weeks ago: 81.0 kg) |
| Neck veins | Distended with head of bed at 45 degrees |
| Ankles | 3+ pitting edema on both sides |

stimuli.title: Case study: urinary sepsis in an older adult
stimuli.text:
Medical unit, 0700. An 81-year-old client from an assisted living facility was admitted overnight with a urinary tract infection. History: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, mild cognitive impairment. Weight 58 kg. Baseline per her daughter: oriented to person and place, follows a conversation, forgets recent events, walks with a walker.

Home medications: metformin 1,000 mg PO twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg PO daily, amlodipine 5 mg PO daily. No known allergies.

| 0700 assessment | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 88/50 mm Hg (home average 142/80) |
| Heart rate | 112/min |
| Respirations | 24/min |
| Temperature | 101.8 F |
| SpO2 | 94% on room air |
| Urine | 60 mL of dark, cloudy urine since 2300 |

The daughter says, "She's not herself. Yesterday she was chatting with me on the phone."

stimuli.title: Case study: diabetic ketoacidosis
stimuli.text:
Emergency department, 2200. A 19-year-old college student with type 1 diabetes comes in with 2 days of vomiting and abdominal pain. The roommate says the client stopped taking insulin glargine 2 days ago "because I wasn't eating." The client is drowsy but answers questions.

| Assessment | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 98/58 mm Hg |
| Heart rate | 124/min |
| Respirations | 32/min, deep |
| Temperature | 99.1 F |
| Weight | 62 kg |
| Bedside glucose | 486 mg/dL |

questions.stem: The nurse receives handoff report on four clients. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: New colostomy client, beefy red stoma
questions.explanation: Wheezing that disappears while SpO2 falls during an asthma attack signals a silent chest from severe airflow obstruction and impending respiratory failure. An SpO2 near 89% is an acceptable target for many clients with COPD, ankle edema is a chronic heart failure finding, and a beefy red stoma is normal.

questions.passage:
| Time | aPTT | Heparin rate |
|---|---|---|
| 0600 | 62 sec | 1,000 units/hr |
| 1200 | 118 sec | 1,000 units/hr |

Control aPTT: 30 sec. No visible bleeding.
questions.stem: A client receives a continuous IV heparin infusion titrated by protocol (goal aPTT 1.5 to 2.5 times control). Based on the 1200 result, which action should the nurse take?
options: Hold the infusion and notify the HCP
questions.explanation: An aPTT of 118 seconds is nearly 4 times control, well above the 45 to 75 second goal, so the infusion is held (protocols then restart it at a lower rate) and the HCP notified because of bleeding risk. Vitamin K reverses warfarin, not heparin; protamine sulfate is the heparin antidote.

questions.stem: The nurse prepares to enter the room of a client on contact and droplet precautions. Place the steps in the order the nurse should perform them.
questions.explanation: The CDC donning sequence is hand hygiene, gown, mask, eye protection, then gloves, so the gloves go on last and cover the gown cuffs. Putting gloves on before the gown leaves the wrists exposed and contaminates the gloves while tying the gown.

questions.stem: Two hours after a cardiac catheterization through the right femoral artery, the nurse finds the dressing saturated and blood pooling under the client's thigh. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Elevate the head of the bed
Recheck the vital signs in 15 minutes
Apply firm pressure above the site
Notify the HCP of the bleeding
questions.explanation: Active arterial bleeding is stopped with direct manual pressure just above the puncture site, then the HCP is notified. Raising the head of the bed flexes the hip and can worsen bleeding, and waiting to recheck vitals delays control of hemorrhage.

| PaCO2 | 58 mm Hg |
| HCO3 | 26 mEq/L |
| PaO2 | 70 mm Hg |
questions.stem: A client receiving morphine by PCA after surgery has a respiratory rate of 8 breaths/min. Which interpretation of the arterial blood gas is correct?
questions.explanation: The pH is low and the PaCO2 is high, so the cause is respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation, and the normal bicarbonate shows the kidneys have not yet compensated. Partial compensation would show a bicarbonate above 26 mEq/L.

| 1500 | 120/76 | 84 | Firm, 2 cm above umbilicus, deviated right | Moderate rubra |
questions.stem: A client is 2 hours postpartum after a vaginal birth. Based on the assessment, which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: A firm fundus that is above the umbilicus and displaced to one side points to a full bladder, so emptying the bladder comes first. Massage is for a boggy fundus, and this one is firm.

questions.stem: A client whose wife died 2 months ago says, "I don't see the point of going on anymore." Which response by the nurse is best?
options: "Things will get easier as time goes by."
"Your children still need you so much."
"Are you thinking of ending your life?"
"Why do you feel there is no point now?"
questions.explanation: A statement of hopelessness calls for a direct question about suicidal thoughts, which does not plant the idea and opens the door to a safety assessment. False reassurance and "why" questions block communication and leave the risk unassessed.

questions.stem: A client with weakness in the left leg is learning to walk with a single-point cane. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: "I'll move the cane with my right leg."
"I'll hold the cane in my right hand."
"I'll hold the cane in my left hand."
"Going down stairs, I'll lead with my right."
questions.explanation: The cane is held on the stronger side (right) and advanced with the weaker leg so it shares that leg's load. Going down stairs, the cane and weaker leg lead, so leading with the stronger right leg is incorrect.

questions.stem: The RN is planning care on a medical-surgical unit. Which tasks can the RN delegate to assistive personnel (AP)? Select all that apply.
options: Obtain vital signs on a stable client
Assess a new stage 2 pressure injury
Help a client with a bed bath
Teach use of an incentive spirometer
questions.explanation: AP can perform routine, standardized tasks for stable clients, such as vital signs, hygiene and measuring intake. Assessing a new pressure injury and teaching require RN judgment and cannot be delegated to AP.

questions.passage:
0800 Nurses' note: Client reports nausea and seeing yellow halos around lights. Apical pulse 54/min, irregular.

| Lab | Result |
|---|---|
| Potassium | 3.0 mEq/L |
| Digoxin | 2.6 ng/mL |
questions.stem: A client with heart failure takes digoxin and furosemide. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: Nausea, yellow halos, bradycardia and a level above 2.0 ng/mL point to digoxin toxicity, so the next dose is withheld before anything else. Furosemide would lower the already low potassium, which worsens toxicity.

questions.stem: A client is admitted with suspected active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which measures should the nurse implement? Select all that apply.
options: Surgical mask on client during transport
Door left open if the client is masked
questions.explanation: Airborne precautions require a negative-pressure isolation room with the door closed, a fit-tested N95 or higher respirator for staff, and a surgical mask on the client outside the room. A surgical mask does not protect staff from airborne droplet nuclei.

questions.stem: The nurse reviews the vital signs of a client who had an abdominal hysterectomy this morning. Complete the sentence. The client is most likely experiencing [[1]], as shown by [[2]].
blanks: a slowing pulse and respiratory rate
questions.explanation: Falling blood pressure and urine output with a rising heart rate and respiratory rate is the pattern of hypovolemia from internal bleeding. Opioid-induced hypotension would come with a slowing pulse and breathing, not tachycardia and tachypnea.

questions.stem: A client arrives at the emergency department with crushing chest pain. SpO2 is 96% on room air. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: A 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival identifies ST-elevation MI, which determines urgent reperfusion. Oxygen is not needed with an SpO2 of 96%, and troponin results take longer and do not replace the ECG.

questions.stem: The charge nurse is making assignments. Which client is most appropriate to assign to the licensed practical nurse (LPN)?
options: Client needing initial teaching on warfarin
Client starting a first unit of packed RBCs
Client with chest pain admitted 30 minutes ago
Client with stable diabetes due for insulin
questions.explanation: An LPN can care for a stable client with a predictable condition, including giving scheduled subcutaneous insulin. A new admission with chest pain needs RN assessment, initial teaching is an RN responsibility, and the start of a transfusion, when reactions are most likely, is monitored by the RN.

questions.stem: The nurse assesses a 12-month-old at a well-child visit. For each finding, specify whether it is expected or requires follow-up.
rows: Does not respond to own name
questions.explanation: Cruising, a first meaningful word, banging blocks together and not yet walking are all expected at 12 months, since walking alone can start as late as 15 months. Sitting without support is expected by about 9 months and responding to one's name by about 9 months, so both need a developmental evaluation.

questions.passage: Day 2, 2200 Nurses' notes: Last drink about 60 hours ago, the night before admission, per the spouse, who reports years of daily heavy drinking. Tremulous and diaphoretic, picking at the sheets, says bugs are crawling on the wall. Disoriented to time and place. BP 172/100 mm Hg, HR 122/min, T 100.6 F, SpO2 97% on room air. No petechiae noted.
questions.stem: A client was admitted 2 days ago with a fractured femur. Complete the diagram by choosing 2 actions the nurse should take, the condition the client is most likely experiencing, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.
questions.explanation: Hallucinations, disorientation, fever and rising vital signs 2 to 3 days after the last drink are alcohol withdrawal delirium, treated with the prescribed benzodiazepine and seizure precautions while vital signs and level of consciousness are watched for worsening. Fat embolism after a femur fracture also causes confusion and fever, but it brings hypoxemia and petechiae, which this client does not have; restraints raise agitation and injury risk.

questions.stem: The nurse prepares to give IV potassium chloride to an adult client through a peripheral line. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Give it by slow IV push
Run it on an infusion pump
Dilute it in IV fluid first
questions.explanation: Potassium is always diluted, pump-controlled, and given only when urine output shows the kidneys can clear it. It is never given by IV push, which can cause fatal dysrhythmias, and peripheral rates are commonly limited to about 10 mEq/hr, so 40 mEq in 30 minutes is far too fast.

questions.passage: Client, 82, 2 days after hip repair. Braden score 12. Incontinent of urine. Eats about half of each meal. Sacral skin intact with blanchable redness.
questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include in this client's plan of care? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the head of bed at 45 degrees
questions.explanation: A Braden score of 12 is high risk, so the plan includes regular repositioning, a pressure redistribution surface and prompt cleansing of moisture. Massaging reddened skin damages tissue, and raising the head of the bed above 30 degrees increases sacral shear.

questions.passage:
Lab result: stool positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin.
Orders: contact precautions. Oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours.
questions.stem: Which action should the nurse take when leaving this client's room after care?
options: Remove the gown in the hallway
Wash hands with soap and water
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not kill C. difficile spores, so hands are washed with soap and water, whose friction and rinsing remove spores. The gown is removed before leaving the room, and shared equipment needs a sporicidal disinfectant such as bleach, not alcohol.

questions.stem: A client scheduled for a colectomy tells the nurse, "I'm not sure what the surgeon is going to remove." The consent form is not yet signed. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Ask the spouse to sign the consent
Explain the procedure to the client
Have the client sign and clarify later
questions.explanation: The surgeon must explain the procedure, risks and alternatives, so the nurse holds the signing and notifies the surgeon when the client lacks understanding. Explaining the surgery is not the nurse's role in consent, which is to witness the signature and confirm the client understands.

questions.stem: A postoperative client receiving IV morphine is difficult to arouse and has a respiratory rate of 7/min. Which medication should the nurse prepare to give?
questions.explanation: Naloxone is the opioid antagonist that reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression. Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines, not opioids.

questions.stem: One hour after a thoracentesis, which finding should the nurse report to the HCP immediately?
questions.explanation: Sudden shortness of breath with falling oxygen saturation after thoracentesis suggests pneumothorax and needs immediate follow-up. Mild site soreness and a small spot of serous drainage are expected after the procedure.

questions.stem: Which findings would the nurse expect in a client with diabetic ketoacidosis? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Kussmaul breathing, a fruity breath odor and a low bicarbonate reflect ketone-driven metabolic acidosis. Very high glucose without ketones describes hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state, and dehydration in DKA causes tachycardia, not bradycardia.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches the parent of a 5-day-old breastfed newborn how to tell whether the infant is feeding well. Which findings indicate adequate intake? Select all that apply.
options: Six or more wet diapers daily
questions.explanation: Six or more wet diapers, audible swallowing and yellow seedy stools by day 5 show good milk transfer. Newborns should feed 8 to 12 times a day, not every 5 to 6 hours, and a loss over 10% of birth weight needs evaluation.

questions.stem: A client who uses heroin daily has had no opioids for 18 hours. Which findings indicate opioid withdrawal? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Yawning, dilated pupils and piloerection are classic signs of opioid withdrawal. Pinpoint pupils and slow, shallow breathing are signs of opioid intoxication, not withdrawal.

questions.passage: Nurses' notes, 0215: 79-year-old client found sitting on the floor beside the bed. States, "I was going to the bathroom." Alert and oriented. Bed alarm was off.
questions.stem: The nurse responds to this fall. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Notify the HCP about the fall
Help the client back into bed
questions.explanation: The nurse checks for injury, such as head trauma or hip pain, before moving the client, because moving an injured client can worsen harm. Helping the client up, notifying the HCP and completing an incident report follow the assessment.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches a client about naming a durable power of attorney for health care. Which client statement indicates understanding?
options: "It only takes effect after I have died."
"My sister will decide for me if I can't decide."
"My sister can overrule me even while I'm alert."
"This also lets my sister pay my bills for me."
questions.explanation: A health care agent makes decisions only when the client cannot, and the client's own choices govern while the client has capacity. Financial matters need a separate financial power of attorney, and the authority ends, rather than begins, at death.

questions.stem: Fifteen minutes into a unit of packed red blood cells, a client reports chills and low back pain. Temperature has risen from 98.8 F to 101.2 F (38.4 C). Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: Chills, fever and back pain early in a transfusion suggest an acute hemolytic reaction, so the transfusion is stopped at once, then the line is kept open with 0.9% saline at a new tubing set. Notifying the blood bank is required, but only after the infusion is stopped.

questions.stem: The nurse inserts a nasogastric tube that will be used for tube feeding. Place the steps in the order the nurse should perform them.
options: Measure nose to earlobe to xiphoid
Lubricate the tip with water-soluble gel
Pass the tube through the nostril
Have the client tuck chin and swallow
Advance the tube to the marked length
questions.explanation: The tube is measured and marked first, lubricated, passed through the nostril to the throat, then advanced to the mark while the client flexes the neck and swallows to close the airway. Placement for feeding is confirmed by x-ray before anything is instilled, because auscultating an air bolus is not reliable.

questions.stem: A client is on the first postoperative day after a total hip replacement. Which actions should the nurse include to reduce the risk of deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
options: Massage the calf if it cramps
Place a pillow under the knees
questions.explanation: Compression devices, ankle pumps and early ambulation all promote venous return. Massaging the calf could dislodge an existing clot, and a pillow under the knees compresses the popliteal veins and slows flow.

questions.stem: The nurse reviews neurologic checks for a client admitted after a fall with a head injury. No opioids have been given. Which problem do these findings most likely indicate?
questions.explanation: Rising systolic pressure with a widening pulse pressure, a slowing pulse and irregular breathing (Cushing triad) with a falling GCS signal increasing intracranial pressure. Hypovolemic shock causes hypotension and tachycardia instead.

questions.stem: Which actions by health care staff violate client confidentiality? Select all that apply.
options: Discussing a client's diagnosis in an elevator
Sharing lab results with a consulting HCP
Giving handoff report in a private area
Posting a photo showing a client's name board
Reviewing the chart of a client in your care
questions.explanation: Talking about a client in a public space and posting images with identifying details are privacy breaches. Sharing results with a treating HCP, private handoff and reviewing the record of an assigned client are permitted uses of information for care.

questions.stem: A client has soft wrist restraints ordered to protect an endotracheal tube. Which actions by the nurse are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Tie the straps to the side rails
questions.explanation: Restraints are secured to the bed frame with a quick-release knot, and the client is released, repositioned and checked at least every 2 hours. Side rails move and can tighten the strap, orders are renewed at least daily under most facility policies, and circulation is checked much more often than once a shift.

questions.stem: Total parenteral nutrition is prescribed at 83 mL/hr. At the start of the shift, the nurse finds the bag is 300 mL behind schedule. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Spread the 300 mL over the shift
Increase the rate to catch up
Stop the bag and hang a new one
questions.explanation: TPN is never sped up to make up lost volume, because a rapid dextrose load can cause hyperglycemia and fluid overload; the nurse keeps the prescribed rate and reports the shortfall. Spreading the missed volume over the shift is still a catch-up increase.

questions.stem: Several clients are due for the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine. For which client should the nurse withhold the vaccine and notify the HCP?
options: Toddler with a cold and no fever
questions.explanation: MMR is a live vaccine and is contraindicated in pregnancy. A mild illness without fever, breastfeeding and egg allergy are not reasons to withhold MMR.

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia stares at an empty corner and says, "Do you hear them too? They're laughing at me." Which response by the nurse is best?
options: "Yes, I hear them. What are they saying?"
"Why would they be laughing at you?"
"Try to ignore them and watch TV."
"I don't hear them, but you look scared."
questions.explanation: The nurse presents reality without arguing and acknowledges the feeling behind the experience. Agreeing reinforces the hallucination, "why" questions ask for an explanation the client cannot give, and telling the client to ignore the voices dismisses them.

questions.stem: A client's 0900 antibiotic was missed and given at 1130. Which statement about the incident report is correct?
options: Chart that an incident report was completed
Have the client sign the completed report
Complete it only if the client is harmed
File it separately from the client's record
questions.explanation: An incident report is a confidential quality improvement document kept out of the medical record, and the chart describes only the facts and the care given, not that a report was filed. Reports are completed for errors and near misses whether or not harm occurred.

questions.passage: 1415 Nurses' note: Sitting upright on the stretcher, {{speaking in 3 to 4 word phrases}}. {{Alert and oriented x4}}. {{Crackles in both lungs to midlung}}. {{SpO2 89% on room air}}. {{Bowel sounds active x4}}. {{Pedal pulses 2+ on both sides}}. {{Weight up 3.5 kg in 2 weeks}}. {{Oral temperature 98.4 F}}.
questions.stem: The nurse completes the initial assessment. Highlight the findings that require follow-up.
questions.explanation: Speaking in short phrases, crackles to midlung, an SpO2 of 89% and a 3.5 kg gain in 2 weeks show pulmonary congestion and fluid retention that need treatment now. Orientation, active bowel sounds, 2+ pedal pulses and a normal temperature are expected and need no follow-up.

questions.passage:
1445 Results:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| BNP | 1,240 pg/mL |
| Potassium | 4.2 mEq/L |
| Chest x-ray | Vascular congestion, small effusions on both sides |
| Troponin I | Within the reference range |
| Hemoglobin | 13.6 g/dL |
questions.stem: For each result, specify whether it is consistent or not consistent with fluid volume overload.
questions.explanation: A BNP far above 100 pg/mL is released by stretched, overloaded ventricles, and vascular congestion with effusions is fluid backing into the lungs. A normal potassium, hemoglobin and troponin do not point to overload; the normal troponin is the tempting one, but it argues against a heart attack, not for fluid excess.

questions.passage: The chest x-ray shows an enlarged heart and vascular congestion with no focal infiltrate. Troponin I is within the reference range.
questions.stem: Complete the sentence. The client's findings are most consistent with [[1]], most likely triggered by [[2]].
blanks: a clot in a pulmonary artery
a reaction to the ACE inhibitor
questions.explanation: Orthopnea, crackles, distended neck veins, edema and a 3.5 kg gain after stopping furosemide and eating high-sodium foods describe acute decompensated heart failure from fluid and sodium retention. Pneumonia is less likely with no fever and no infiltrate, and a normal troponin argues against a heart attack.

questions.stem: The client is admitted to the cardiac unit. Which interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care? Select all that apply.
options: Raise the head of the bed high
Offer 3 L of oral fluids daily
Elevate both legs above the heart
Limit sodium to 2 g per day
questions.explanation: High Fowler's eases breathing, a daily weight on the same scale before breakfast tracks fluid, and a 2 g sodium limit reduces fluid retention. Pushing 3 L of fluid adds to the overload, and raising the legs above the heart returns more blood to an already congested heart and lungs.

questions.passage:
1800: After the first dose of IV furosemide the client has voided 900 mL. BP 142/86 mm Hg, HR 98/min, SpO2 93% on 2 L/min by nasal cannula.

| Lab | Result |
|---|---|
| Potassium | 3.2 mEq/L |
| Creatinine | 1.6 mg/dL (1.5 on arrival, baseline 1.1) |
questions.stem: The nurse reviews the admission prescriptions. For each prescription, specify whether the nurse should give it as prescribed or clarify it with the HCP.
questions.explanation: Furosemide is working and still needed because the creatinine was already up from congestion on arrival, potassium 3.2 mEq/L needs replacement, and enoxaparin prevents clots in a hospitalized client with limited mobility. Metformin is held in an acutely ill client with hypoxemia and a creatinine above baseline because of lactic acidosis risk, and a continuous IV at 125 mL/hr adds volume to a client being treated for overload.

questions.passage: Day 3, 0800: Weight 81.4 kg. Lungs clear. SpO2 95% on room air. Sleeps on one pillow. 3+ pitting edema of both ankles. The client says, "Once my ankles look normal, I can stop the water pill."
questions.stem: The nurse evaluates the client's response to treatment before discharge. For each finding, specify whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.
rows: Plans to stop the water pill
questions.explanation: A 3.1 kg weight loss, sleeping flat on one pillow and a normal SpO2 on room air show the congestion has resolved. Ankle edema unchanged at 3+ still needs follow-up, and planning to stop furosemide when the ankles improve is a teaching gap that could cause another admission.

questions.stem: Before giving a medication, which pair of identifiers should the nurse use?
options: Full name and date of birth
Name on the door and chart
questions.explanation: Two person-specific identifiers, such as full name and date of birth or medical record number, are checked against the wristband and the MAR. A room or bed number is never an identifier because clients move.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches sleep hygiene to a client with insomnia. Which statement indicates a need for further teaching?
options: "I'll get up at the same time each day."
"I'll get out of bed if I can't sleep."
"I'll watch TV in bed until I'm sleepy."
questions.explanation: The bed should be linked only with sleep, and screen light delays sleep onset. A fixed wake time, avoiding afternoon caffeine and leaving the bed after about 20 minutes awake are all correct sleep hygiene.

questions.stem: During an IV vancomycin infusion, a client develops flushing and a red rash on the face, neck, and upper chest. BP is 118/76 mm Hg, and the lungs are clear with no stridor. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: Flushing and an upper-body rash during infusion with stable vital signs is vancomycin infusion reaction, usually from running it too fast; the infusion is stopped, and it is later resumed more slowly, often after an antihistamine. Epinephrine is for anaphylaxis, which this stable client without airway signs does not show.

questions.stem: A client with ascites is scheduled for a paracentesis. Which action should the nurse take just before the procedure?
options: Keep the client NPO for 12 hours
Position the client supine and flat
Have the client empty the bladder
questions.explanation: Emptying the bladder lowers the risk of puncturing it when the needle enters the lower abdomen. The client sits upright or in high Fowler's position, not flat, and fasting and an enema are not required.

questions.stem: A client has sudden right-sided facial droop and slurred speech. Which information is most important for the nurse to obtain first?
questions.explanation: The time the client was last known to be normal determines eligibility for thrombolytic and clot-retrieval therapy, so it is gathered immediately. Family and smoking history are risk factors that do not change acute treatment.

questions.stem: The nurse calls the HCP about a client with a possible postoperative bleed using SBAR. Which statement belongs in the Recommendation?
options: "I think he may be bleeding internally."
"I'm calling about Mr. Lee in room 4."
questions.explanation: The Recommendation states what the nurse needs, such as a bedside evaluation within a set time. The other statements are the Situation, Background and Assessment.

questions.stem: The nurse assesses a 78-year-old client at an annual wellness visit. Which findings are expected age-related changes? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Loss of skin elasticity and needing more light to read are normal with aging. Confusion that develops over days suggests delirium, a heart rate of 44 is bradycardia, and urinating 12 times a day suggests infection or another disorder, so none of these should be dismissed as aging.

questions.stem: The nurse assesses a 2-year-old brought to the emergency department after a fall. Which finding is most suggestive of physical abuse?
questions.explanation: Patterned loop marks suggest a cord or belt, and the back is not a typical site for accidental injury. Bruised shins, scraped palms and knees and forehead bumps are common accidental injuries in a toddler who is learning to run.

questions.stem: A client starting phenelzine asks which foods to avoid. Which foods should the nurse list? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Aged cheese, cured meats and tap beer are high in tyramine, which can trigger hypertensive crisis with an MAOI. Freshly cooked chicken and fresh, unaged cheeses such as cottage cheese are low in tyramine.

questions.stem: At a mass casualty scene, the nurse uses START triage. Which adult should be tagged immediate (red)?
options: Apneic after the airway is repositioned
Walking and talking, deep arm cut
RR 24, cap refill 1 s, obeys commands
RR 34, cap refill 1 s, obeys commands
questions.explanation: In START, a respiratory rate over 30 earns an immediate (red) tag even when perfusion and mental status are normal. The victim with RR 24, brisk capillary refill and who obeys commands is delayed (yellow), the walking victim is minor (green), and no breathing after repositioning the airway is expectant (black).

questions.passage:
| Client | Report from night nurse |
|---|---|
| A, 4 hours after thyroidectomy | Hoarse voice, noisy breathing |
| B, cellulitis of the leg | Temperature 100.6 F |
| C, heart failure | Weight up 0.5 kg since yesterday |
| D, appendectomy yesterday | Incision pain 6/10 |
questions.stem: The nurse reviews the night nurse's report. Which client should the nurse see first?
questions.explanation: Hoarseness with noisy breathing after a thyroidectomy suggests laryngeal edema or nerve injury and an airway at risk, which comes first. A low-grade fever with cellulitis, a small weight gain and expected incision pain need attention but do not threaten the airway.

questions.stem: A client is back on the unit after an upper endoscopy (EGD) with moderate sedation and asks for something to drink. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Give warm tea for the throat
questions.explanation: The throat is anesthetized for the procedure, so the gag reflex must return before any fluids, including ice chips, to prevent aspiration. Offering sips first skips that safety check.

questions.stem: A client with pneumonia has received a 30 mL/kg fluid bolus. Which findings support a diagnosis of septic shock? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Septic shock is hypotension needing vasopressors to keep MAP at 65 or above despite fluids, with signs of poor perfusion such as high lactate, low urine output and altered mental status. A capillary refill of 2 seconds is normal.

questions.stem: The nurse observes a client using axillary crutches. Which observation indicates correct crutch fit and use?
options: Tips placed 1 inch beside each foot
questions.explanation: Pads should sit 1.5 to 2 inches (2 to 3 finger widths) below the axillae with weight on the hands, which prevents brachial nerve injury. Elbows should flex about 20 to 30 degrees, and tips sit about 6 inches in front of and beside the feet.

questions.stem: A client with heart failure received IV furosemide 40 mg this morning. Which findings indicate the medication is effective? Select all that apply.
options: Fewer crackles in the lung bases
questions.explanation: Weight loss and clearing crackles show fluid removal. Potassium 3.2 mEq/L is an adverse effect, not a sign of benefit; new edema and urine output of 20 mL/hr show the diuretic is not working.

questions.stem: A client being treated for pneumonia tells the nurse, "I'm leaving now, I don't care what the doctor says." Which action is appropriate?
options: Keep the client's clothes until the HCP comes
Apply restraints until the HCP arrives
Tell the client insurance will not pay
Notify the HCP and explain the risks
questions.explanation: A competent adult may leave against medical advice, so the nurse explains the risks, notifies the HCP and asks the client to sign the AMA form. Holding belongings or restraining the client is false imprisonment, and warning about insurance is a misleading pressure tactic.

questions.stem: The nurse is setting up a sterile field for a dressing change. Which actions contaminate the field? Select all that apply.
options: Holding sterile items below the waist
Turning away from the sterile field
Setting a wet item on a sterile drape
questions.explanation: Items below waist level or out of sight are considered contaminated, reaching over the field can drop particles onto it, and moisture wicks microorganisms through the drape. Treating the outer 1-inch border as nonsterile is correct technique.

questions.passage: Newborn at 1 minute: heart rate 110 beats/min, slow irregular breathing with a weak cry, some flexion of the arms and legs, grimaces when the soles are flicked, body pink with blue hands and feet.
questions.stem: Based on the 1-minute assessment, what Apgar score should the nurse record?
questions.explanation: Heart rate over 100 scores 2; slow, weak cry 1; some flexion 1; grimace 1; pink body with blue extremities 1, for a total of 6. A score of 7 would require one more point, such as active motion or a vigorous cry.

questions.passage: Day 12 Nurses' note: Client with major depression began sertraline 12 days ago. After a week of staying in bed, today she is {{smiling and energetic}}. {{Gave her watch and family photos to her sister}}. {{Ate all of breakfast and lunch}}. Says, {{"Everything is settled now."}} {{Attended group therapy this morning}}. {{Slept 7 hours last night}}.
questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest an increased risk of suicide.
questions.explanation: A sudden lift in mood and energy early in antidepressant therapy, giving away valued belongings and saying everything is settled can mean the client has made a suicide plan and now has the energy to act on it. Eating, attending group and sleeping 7 hours are true improvements and do not by themselves raise concern.

questions.stem: A client is on day 5 of a continuous heparin infusion for a deep vein thrombosis. Which finding requires immediate follow-up?
questions.explanation: A platelet drop of more than 50% from baseline 5 to 10 days after starting heparin suggests heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, which needs the heparin stopped and the HCP notified. An aPTT of 68 seconds is within a typical therapeutic range, so it is not the concern.

questions.stem: A 70 kg adult has partial- and full-thickness burns over 40% of the body. The HCP prescribes lactated Ringer's at 4 mL/kg/%TBSA over 24 hours using the Parkland formula. How many mL should the client receive in the first 8 hours after the burn? Record your answer as a whole number without commas.
questions.explanation: The 24-hour total is 4 x 70 x 40 = 11,200 mL, and half of it, 5,600 mL, is given in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn. 11,200 mL is the full-day total, not the first 8 hours.

questions.stem: A heparin infusion of 25,000 units in 250 mL D5W is prescribed to run at 1,200 units/hr. At what rate in mL/hr should the nurse set the infusion pump? Record your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: The concentration is 25,000 units / 250 mL = 100 units/mL, and 1,200 units/hr / 100 units/mL = 12 mL/hr. 120 mL/hr comes from a decimal error and would deliver ten times the dose.

questions.stem: A nurse supports a competent client's decision to stop dialysis, although the nurse believes dialysis would help. Which ethical principle is the nurse upholding?
questions.explanation: Autonomy is the client's right to make informed choices about their own care, including refusing treatment. Beneficence, doing good, is the principle the nurse sets aside here in favor of the client's choice.

questions.stem: A cleaning chemical splashes into a nurse's eye. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Cover the eye with a dry gauze pad
Flush the eye at an eyewash station
Find the safety data sheet for it
questions.explanation: Immediate irrigation, generally for at least 15 minutes, limits tissue damage from a chemical splash. The safety data sheet and an occupational health report are important next steps but must not delay flushing.

questions.stem: A client with heart failure is prescribed a 2 g sodium diet. Which foods are appropriate choices? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Fresh fruit and oatmeal cooked without salt are naturally low in sodium. Canned soups, pickles and deli meats are among the highest-sodium foods.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches a client starting oral phenytoin for a seizure disorder. Which instructions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
options: Double the next dose if missed
Take it with an antacid dose
questions.explanation: Phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia, has a narrow therapeutic range (about 10 to 20 mcg/mL), and interacts with alcohol. Antacids reduce its absorption and should be separated by about 2 hours, and doubling a dose risks toxicity.

questions.stem: A client in active labor is receiving an oxytocin infusion. The fetal monitor shows recurrent late decelerations with minimal variability. Complete the sentence. This pattern most often reflects [[1]], so the nurse should first [[2]].
questions.explanation: Late decelerations mean the placenta is not delivering enough oxygen during contractions, and oxytocin strengthens contractions, so stopping it is the first step of intrauterine resuscitation. Cord compression causes variable decelerations, not late ones, and waiting an hour delays care for a fetus that may be hypoxic.

questions.stem: A client in an acute manic episode is pacing the unit and talking rapidly. Which activity should the nurse suggest?
questions.explanation: A noncompetitive physical activity with one staff member uses excess energy with little stimulation. Team and competitive games overstimulate, and a client in acute mania cannot concentrate on a novel.

questions.stem: The RN is working with a licensed practical nurse (LPN) on a medical unit. Which tasks are appropriate to assign to the LPN? Select all that apply.
options: Reinforce teaching on a low-sodium diet
Change a dressing on a stable wound
Teach a new diabetic to self-inject
questions.explanation: LPNs can reinforce teaching the RN has started, give scheduled oral medications and do routine dressing changes on stable clients. The admission assessment and initial teaching for a new diagnosis require the RN.

questions.stem: On the first day after abdominal surgery, a client has a temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) and diminished breath sounds in both bases. Which action should the nurse take?
questions.explanation: A low-grade fever with diminished bases in the first 24 to 48 hours after surgery most often reflects atelectasis, which is treated with deep breathing and incentive spirometry. Blood cultures are not the first step for this pattern this early after surgery.

questions.stem: A client has a chest tube to suction for a pneumothorax. The nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Strip the tubing toward the drain
Document it as an expected finding
questions.explanation: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber signals an air leak, which is most often a loose connection in the system, so the nurse checks from the dressing to the drain. Intermittent bubbling with exhalation or coughing is expected, but continuous bubbling is not.

questions.stem: A client has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure while in bed. For each action, specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated during the seizure.
rows: Turn the client onto one side
questions.explanation: Side-lying keeps the airway clear, timing the seizure guides treatment, and loosening tight clothing eases breathing. Nothing goes into the mouth during a seizure, including an airway or glucose gel, and holding the limbs can cause fractures.

questions.stem: A client's peripheral IV of 0.9% sodium chloride is running. The site is cool, pale, and swollen. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Elevate the arm on a pillow
Flush the line to test it
questions.explanation: Cool, pale, swollen tissue signals infiltration, so the infusion is stopped first and the catheter then removed. Elevating the arm and applying a compress come after, and flushing pushes more fluid into the tissue.

questions.explanation: A drop in BP to 92/54 with a heart rate of 116, urine output under 30 mL/hr and new restlessness are signs of hypovolemia or bleeding that the AP must report immediately. The 0800 vital signs, mild pain and taking half of a clear liquid tray are expected the day after surgery.

questions.passage: 1400 Nurses' note: Client 6 hours after hip surgery under spinal anesthesia. Has not voided since surgery. Reports lower abdominal fullness. Bladder scan shows 650 mL.
questions.stem: The client tried to void with privacy, sitting upright, and running water but could not. Which action should the nurse take next?
questions.explanation: A bladder volume of 650 mL with failed voiding attempts calls for intermittent catheterization to relieve retention. An indwelling catheter adds infection risk without need, and more fluid or waiting further distends the bladder.

questions.stem: The nurse is performing an abdominal assessment on an adult client. Which technique should the nurse perform first?
questions.explanation: The abdomen is assessed in the order inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation. Auscultation comes second, before touching the abdomen can alter bowel sounds.

questions.stem: A client whose spouse died 3 weeks ago reports crying daily, poor sleep and sometimes hearing the spouse's voice at night. How should the nurse interpret these findings?
questions.explanation: Sadness, sleep changes and briefly sensing or hearing the deceased are common in the early weeks of grief. Prolonged grief is not considered until symptoms persist about a year in adults, and the voice here does not make the client psychotic.

questions.stem: Four hours after a cardiac catheterization through the left femoral artery, which findings require immediate follow-up? Select all that apply.
options: Small bruise at the insertion site
Absent pedal pulse in left foot
questions.explanation: An absent pulse and a cool, pale foot suggest arterial occlusion, and new back or flank pain can signal a retroperitoneal bleed. A small bruise is expected, and increased urine output reflects the osmotic effect of contrast and the IV fluids given to clear it.

questions.passage: 0300: High-pressure alarm sounding on the ventilator. Client coughing and restless. Coarse rhonchi over the trachea and both upper lobes. SpO2 91%, down from 96%.
questions.stem: The nurse responds to a ventilator alarm. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: A high-pressure alarm with coughing and coarse rhonchi points to secretions blocking the airway, which suctioning clears. A disconnection causes a low-pressure alarm, and raising the tidal volume would raise airway pressure further.

questions.passage: Mobility assessment: 58-year-old client, 118 kg. Cannot bear weight on either leg. Needs help to sit up and has poor trunk control. Follows commands. Order: out of bed to chair twice daily.
questions.stem: Which method should the nurse use to move this client from the bed to a chair?
options: Powered sit-to-stand lift with one staff
Two-person pivot with a gait belt
Slide board with one staff member
Full-body mechanical lift and two staff
questions.explanation: A client who cannot bear weight and has poor trunk control needs a full-body mechanical lift operated by at least two staff to protect both client and staff. A sit-to-stand lift and pivot transfers require partial weight bearing, and a slide board requires trunk control.

questions.stem: A client with preeclampsia receives magnesium sulfate 2 g/hr IV. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.explanation: Absent reflexes, a respiratory rate of 10/min and a level of 9.2 mg/dL (therapeutic about 4 to 7 mg/dL) show magnesium toxicity, so the infusion is stopped first. Calcium gluconate is the antidote and is given next, but continuing the infusion while preparing it adds more drug.

questions.stem: A unit's quality improvement team is tracking fall prevention. Which measure is an outcome measure?
options: Percent of clients screened for fall risk
Number of bed alarms on the unit
questions.explanation: Outcome measures track results for clients, such as the fall rate. The percent of clients screened is a process measure, and equipment and staff training are structure measures.

questions.stem: After change-of-shift report, which client should the nurse assess first?
options: Client with dementia calling out for family
Post-MI client with new crackles and dyspnea
Sickle cell client reporting pain of 7/10
questions.explanation: New dyspnea and crackles after an MI suggest acute heart failure or pulmonary edema, a breathing problem that comes first. Sickle cell pain needs prompt treatment next, and the elevated glucose and calling out are not immediately life-threatening.

Client, 74, takes warfarin 5 mg daily for atrial fibrillation.

Lab: INR 6.8.
questions.stem: The HCP prescribes the reversal agent for this client's anticoagulant. Which medication should the nurse expect?
questions.explanation: Phytonadione restores vitamin K-dependent clotting factors and reverses warfarin; with an INR of 6.8 and only minor bleeding, warfarin is held and a low oral dose is typical. Protamine reverses heparin, idarucizumab reverses dabigatran, and andexanet alfa reverses factor Xa inhibitors.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include to reduce fall risk for a client with dementia? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the bed low with wheels locked
Raise all four side rails at night
Apply a vest restraint during sleep
questions.explanation: A low, locked bed, scheduled toileting and nonskid footwear address common causes of falls. Four raised rails and a vest restraint are restraints that increase injury when a confused client climbs over or struggles against them.

questions.stem: A client who takes metformin is scheduled for a CT scan with IV contrast. Which laboratory result is most important for the nurse to review before the scan?
questions.explanation: Contrast can injure the kidneys, and metformin with poor kidney clearance raises the risk of lactic acidosis, so creatinine and eGFR guide whether metformin is held. Hemoglobin A1c reflects long-term glucose control and does not affect contrast safety.

questions.stem: A client has had nasogastric suction for 3 days after bowel surgery. Complete the sentence. The arterial blood gas shows [[1]] that is [[2]].
questions.explanation: A high pH with a high bicarbonate is metabolic alkalosis from losing gastric acid, and a PaCO2 above 45 shows the lungs retaining CO2 to compensate while the pH is still abnormal, so it is partly compensated. It would be uncompensated if the PaCO2 were still 35 to 45, and fully compensated only if the pH were back in range.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old client with average risk who has never smoked asks which screenings are recommended. Which screenings should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Colorectal screening from age 45, periodic blood pressure checks and a one-time hepatitis C test for adults 18 to 79 are recommended. Chest x-rays are not a screening tool, and routine whole-body skin exams lack evidence for average-risk adults.

questions.stem: Which action by a client using a standard walker indicates correct technique?
options: Pushes off chair arms to stand
Keeps walker a long stride ahead
Pulls up on the walker to stand
questions.explanation: The client pushes up from the chair arms, then grips the walker once standing, because a walker tips when pulled on. The walker is moved about one step ahead and the client steps into it, not past the front bar.

questions.stem: A client just diagnosed with cancer says, "I don't know how I'm going to tell my kids." Which response by the nurse is best?
options: "It may be best to wait until treatment ends."
"What worries you most about telling them?"
"Your HCP can tell them for you if you like."
questions.explanation: An open-ended question invites the client to explore the concern. The other replies reassure, advise or take over the task without learning what the client fears.

questions.stem: The RN supervises an AP caring for a client 2 days after hip replacement. Which statement by the AP requires the RN to intervene?
options: "I'll help him to the chair with his walker."
"I'll hang his next bag of IV fluids now."
"I'll tell you if his heart rate is over 100."
"I'll keep the pillow between his knees."
questions.explanation: Hanging IV fluids is outside the AP's scope, so the RN stops the AP and does it. Assisting with ambulation, reporting vital sign changes and keeping the abduction pillow in place are appropriate AP actions.

questions.stem: The nurse will give regular and NPH insulin in one syringe. Place the steps in the order the nurse should perform them.
options: Roll the NPH vial between the palms
Inject air into the NPH vial
Inject air into the regular vial
questions.explanation: NPH is rolled to mix it, air goes into the NPH vial first and then into the regular vial, and the clear regular insulin is withdrawn before the cloudy NPH. Drawing NPH first would risk pushing intermediate-acting insulin into the regular vial.

questions.stem: Which restraint monitoring finding requires the nurse's immediate action?
options: Straps tied to the bed frame
Client asking for a drink of water
questions.explanation: A cool hand with delayed capillary refill means the restraint is impairing circulation, so the nurse loosens it and reassesses at once. A two-finger fit and tying to the frame are correct practice, and the request for water is met after circulation is restored.

questions.passage: 0630 Nurses' note: Total thyroidectomy 18 hours ago. Client reports tingling around the lips and in both hands. The face twitches when the cheek is tapped, and the hand spasms while the BP cuff is inflated. Voice slightly hoarse, speaking in full sentences. Drain has 20 mL serosanguineous fluid. T 98.8 F, HR 88/min.
questions.stem: Complete the diagram by choosing 2 actions the nurse should take, the condition the client is most likely experiencing, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

groups.label: Actions to take
options: Apply an ice pack to the neck
Lay the client flat without pillows

questions.explanation: Perioral and hand tingling with positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs mean hypocalcemia from parathyroid injury, so the surgeon is notified, IV calcium gluconate is kept ready, and calcium and the airway are watched because laryngospasm can follow. Thyroid storm would bring fever and tachycardia, and mild hoarseness while speaking in full sentences is common after this surgery and does not explain the tingling and spasms.

questions.stem: A client with COPD and chronic CO2 retention is admitted with an exacerbation. Which SpO2 range should the nurse aim for when adjusting oxygen?
questions.explanation: A target of 88% to 92% gives adequate oxygenation while limiting the risk of worsening CO2 retention in clients who retain CO2. The 94% to 98% target applies to most other adults.

questions.stem: Before a client signs a consent for surgery, which conditions must be met? Select all that apply.
options: The client is an adult or emancipated
The client is not impaired by sedatives
The HCP has explained risks and options
The family agrees with the decision
The nurse has explained the procedure
questions.explanation: Valid consent requires legal age or emancipation, capacity free of impairing medication, and disclosure of risks, benefits and alternatives by the HCP. Family agreement is not required for a competent adult, and explaining the procedure is the HCP's duty, not the nurse's.

questions.stem: The nurse assesses a newborn at 4 hours of age. For each finding, specify whether it is expected or should be reported to the HCP.
questions.explanation: A heart rate of 140, acrocyanosis and milia are normal in the first day. A respiratory rate above 60/min and expiratory grunting are signs of respiratory distress that need evaluation.

questions.passage: Wound note: Sacrum, 3 cm x 2 cm shallow open area. Wound bed pink and moist. No slough, no eschar, no visible fat.
questions.stem: How should the nurse document this wound?
questions.explanation: Partial-thickness skin loss with a pink, moist bed and no slough or visible fat is Stage 2. Stage 1 is intact skin, and Stage 3 shows full-thickness loss with visible fat.

questions.stem: The nurse reviews a morphine patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump with a client's family. Which statement by the family indicates a need for further teaching?
options: "We'll tell you if he gets hard to wake up."
"We'll press the button when he's asleep."
"He should press it before pain gets severe."
"The pump limits how much he gets each hour."
questions.explanation: Only the client should press the PCA button; the safety of PCA depends on a sedated client being unable to dose himself, and "PCA by proxy" causes overdoses. Pressing before pain becomes severe is correct teaching.

questions.stem: A client is having a panic attack in the clinic waiting room. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Move to a quiet, dim area
Ask what set off the attack
questions.explanation: During severe anxiety the nurse stays, speaks in short calm statements and reduces stimulation. A client in panic cannot learn new skills or analyze triggers; those wait until anxiety has eased.

questions.stem: A client is admitted with suspected meningococcal meningitis. Which precaution should the nurse implement?
options: Surgical mask on entering the room
Fit-tested N95 for all room entry
Gown and gloves for any contact
questions.explanation: Neisseria meningitidis spreads by large droplets, so droplet precautions with a surgical mask are used until the client has had 24 hours of effective antibiotics. An N95 and a negative-pressure room are for airborne diseases such as tuberculosis, measles and varicella.

questions.passage: Nurses' notes, 0300: 81-year-old client with end-stage COPD, unresponsive, RR 8/min, SpO2 78%. Chart contains a signed living will refusing intubation and mechanical ventilation. Daughter at bedside: "Do whatever it takes. Put her on a breathing machine."
questions.stem: Based on the nurses' notes and the living will, which action should the nurse take?
options: Prepare for intubation as the daughter asks
Ask the daughter to sign intubation consent
Start bag-mask breathing until HCP decides
Honor the living will and notify the HCP
questions.explanation: A valid living will states the client's own wishes and is followed even when family disagrees; the nurse notifies the HCP so orders match it and keeps the client comfortable. The daughter cannot override the client's documented refusal, and bag-mask ventilation is the assisted breathing the client declined.

questions.stem: Before starting a unit of packed red blood cells, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Plan to infuse it over 6 hours
Use a filtered blood tubing set
Check the unit with a second nurse
questions.explanation: Dual verification, saline priming, a filtered blood set and baseline vital signs are all required before a transfusion. A unit should finish within 4 hours of leaving the blood bank, so a 6-hour plan raises bacterial growth risk.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child is 8 hours past a tonsillectomy. Which finding should the nurse report to the HCP?
questions.explanation: Frequent swallowing suggests blood trickling down the back of the throat and is an early sign of hemorrhage. Ear pain is common referred pain after tonsillectomy, and refusing rough food is expected.

questions.stem: Which findings would the nurse expect in a client with syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Excess ADH retains free water, causing dilutional hyponatremia, concentrated urine and weight gain without edema. Large volumes of dilute urine describe diabetes insipidus, and serum osmolality is low, not high, in SIADH.

questions.stem: A client at 30 weeks of gestation calls the clinic. Which report requires immediate follow-up?
questions.explanation: Headache with visual changes can signal preeclampsia with severe features and needs prompt evaluation. Dependent ankle edema, heartburn and painless Braxton Hicks contractions are common in the third trimester.

questions.stem: The nurse observes an AP assisting a client with dysphagia after a stroke during lunch. Which action by the AP requires the nurse to intervene?
options: Offers small bites of soft food
Has the client tuck chin to swallow
questions.explanation: A client with dysphagia should sit fully upright, near 90 degrees, to protect the airway. Small bites, the chin-tuck swallow and checking the weak side for pocketed food are all correct.

questions.stem: After caring for a client on contact and droplet precautions, the nurse removes PPE. Place the steps in the order the nurse should perform them.
options: Remove the gown, rolling it inward
Remove the mask by the ties
questions.explanation: The CDC doffing sequence removes the most contaminated item first: gloves, then eye protection, then the gown, then the mask by its ties, followed by hand hygiene. Taking the mask off before the gown brings contaminated hands near the face.

questions.stem: A caller says he is a client's son and asks how the client's surgery went. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Hand the call to the charge nurse to answer
Give a brief update, since he is family
Verify he is on the client's contact list
Say there is no such client on the unit
questions.explanation: Information is released only to people the client has authorized, often confirmed with a privacy code, so the nurse checks that first. Being a relative does not by itself give a right to health information, and passing the call along does not settle the privacy question.

questions.stem: While the nurse changes a central venous catheter cap, the client suddenly becomes short of breath with chest pain and hypotension. After clamping the catheter, how should the nurse position the client?
questions.explanation: These signs suggest air embolism; the left lateral, head-down position helps trap air in the right atrium away from the pulmonary outflow. Right side-lying moves the air toward the pulmonary artery.

questions.stem: A client on the mental health unit is pacing, shouting and clenching both fists but has not hit anyone. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Leave the client alone to calm
questions.explanation: Verbal de-escalation is the least restrictive intervention and comes first when the client is escalating but not yet violent. Medication and restraints are used only if less restrictive measures fail, and leaving the client removes support and monitoring.

questions.stem: The nurse prepares a client for an MRI of the brain. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Ask about fear of closed spaces
Shave the scalp over the area
questions.explanation: Implanted devices, jewelry and foil-backed medication patches can be pulled or heated by the magnet, and claustrophobia may require sedation or an open scanner. A 24-hour fast is not required, and shaving has no role in MRI.

questions.stem: A client has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 190 beats/min. BP is 118/76 mm Hg, and the client is alert and reports palpitations. Which intervention should the nurse anticipate first?
questions.explanation: Stable supraventricular tachycardia is treated first with vagal maneuvers, then adenosine if they fail. Synchronized cardioversion is for a client who is unstable, with hypotension, chest pain or altered mental status.

questions.stem: A nurse sees a coworker put a client's prescribed oxycodone tablet into her own pocket. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Count the opioids in the cabinet tonight
Report it to the nurse manager at once
Talk with the coworker privately first
Watch for a second incident before acting
questions.explanation: Suspected drug diversion endangers clients and is reported promptly through the chain of command, which protects clients and gets the coworker help. A private talk or waiting for more evidence delays action and leaves clients at risk.

questions.stem: A nursing home resident with an indwelling urinary catheter is on enhanced barrier precautions. For which activities should staff wear a gown and gloves? Select all that apply.
options: Handing the resident a meal tray
Transferring the resident to a chair
questions.explanation: Enhanced barrier precautions call for a gown and gloves during high-contact care such as bathing, transfers, changing linens and device care, when hands and clothing can pick up multidrug-resistant organisms. Brief contact like delivering a tray needs only standard precautions.

questions.stem: A client receives IV gentamicin every 8 hours. Which findings should the nurse report as possible adverse effects? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Tinnitus signals ototoxicity and a rising creatinine signals nephrotoxicity, the two key aminoglycoside toxicities. Urine output of 60 mL/hr and BUN of 14 mg/dL are normal, and a gentamicin trough below 1 to 2 mcg/mL is acceptable.

questions.stem: The nurse reviews laboratory results for a client who gave birth yesterday. Which action is indicated?
options: Give Rh immune globulin to the newborn
Withhold it since the Coombs is negative
Give Rh immune globulin to the client
No Rh immune globulin is needed
questions.explanation: An Rh-negative client who is not sensitized (negative indirect Coombs) and has an Rh-positive newborn should receive Rh immune globulin within 72 hours. The negative Coombs is the reason to give it, not to withhold it, and the medication is never given to the newborn.

questions.stem: A client sprained an ankle 2 hours ago. Which comfort measure should the nurse recommend now?
options: Apply a heating pad on low
Soak the ankle in warm water
Apply ice wrapped in a towel
questions.explanation: Cold in the first 24 to 48 hours limits swelling and pain by vasoconstriction; it is wrapped to protect the skin. Heat in the acute phase increases swelling.

questions.stem: A client had abdominal surgery yesterday. The nurse calls the surgeon using SBAR. Which recommendation is most appropriate?
options: Request vital sign checks every 4 hours
Request an increase in the IV morphine dose
Request a urinalysis and urine culture
Request bedside evaluation and a stat CBC
questions.explanation: Falling BP, rising heart and respiratory rates, and dropping urine output point to hypovolemia, possibly from bleeding, so the nurse asks for prompt evaluation and labs. Less frequent vital signs or more opioid would delay care or worsen hypotension, and the low urine output reflects poor perfusion, not infection.

questions.passage: 0730 Nurses' note: {{Oriented to person only}}. {{Recognizes her daughter}}. {{Loses track of questions mid-sentence}}. {{Cannot recall what she ate yesterday}}. {{Uses her walker to stand}}. {{Alternates between drowsy and agitated}}. {{Speech clear}}.
questions.stem: The nurse compares this assessment with the baseline the daughter describes. Highlight the findings that represent an acute change from baseline.
questions.explanation: Losing orientation to place, being unable to hold attention and a level of alertness that swings between drowsy and agitated are new since yesterday and point to delirium, often the first sign of sepsis in an older adult. Forgetting recent events and using a walker are part of her baseline, and recognizing her daughter and clear speech are reassuring.

questions.stem: For each laboratory result, specify whether it is consistent or not consistent with sepsis.
questions.explanation: Leukocytosis shows infection, a lactate above 2 mmol/L shows tissue hypoperfusion, and creatinine doubled from baseline shows kidney injury from poor perfusion. Sodium, hemoglobin and platelets are normal; a falling platelet count would suggest sepsis, but 245,000 does not.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence. The client is most likely developing [[1]], and the greatest immediate risk is [[2]].
questions.explanation: A urinary infection with fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension, new confusion, a high lactate and rising creatinine is sepsis with organ dysfunction, which can progress to septic shock. Dehydration alone would not explain the fever and high white count, and the BP is far below her baseline, not high.

questions.stem: The nurse notifies the HCP. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Sepsis care starts with blood cultures drawn before a broad-spectrum antibiotic given within the first hour and a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus for hypotension and a high lactate. Lisinopril and furosemide both lower blood pressure and volume in a client who is already hypotensive.

questions.passage: 0930: Blood cultures were drawn at 0905. The crystalloid bolus is infusing. BP 86/48 mm Hg, HR 116/min.
questions.stem: The nurse reviews the client's prescriptions. For each prescription, specify whether the nurse should implement it or hold it and clarify with the HCP.
questions.explanation: The antibiotic is given now that cultures are drawn, the bolus is 30 mL/kg for a 58 kg client, and subcutaneous heparin prevents clots in an immobile client with normal platelets and is safe with her poor kidney function. Lisinopril and amlodipine would deepen the hypotension, and metformin is held because a high lactate and acute kidney injury raise the risk of lactic acidosis.

questions.passage: 1500 Nurses' note: After the fluid bolus and the first antibiotic dose, {{BP 112/64 mm Hg}}, {{HR 96/min}}, {{T 99.8 F}}. {{Urine 25 mL in the last 2 hours}}. Repeat {{lactate 3.9 mmol/L}}. {{Crackles in both lung bases}}, {{SpO2 89% on 2 L/min}}. {{Oriented to person and place}}.
questions.stem: The nurse evaluates the client's response to treatment. Highlight the findings that require follow-up.
questions.explanation: Urine output under 0.5 mL/kg/hr (29 mL/hr for 58 kg) and a lactate that rose from 3.4 show perfusion is still poor, while new crackles and an SpO2 of 89% suggest the fluid is overloading her lungs. The improved BP, heart rate and temperature and a return to her baseline orientation show partial response and do not need escalation on their own.

questions.stem: A client has a sealed radioactive implant for cervical cancer. For each nursing action, specify whether it is appropriate or inappropriate.
rows: Keep a lead container in the room
Pick up a loose implant by hand
Rotate nurses assigned to the client
Let a pregnant sister visit briefly
Wear a dosimeter badge during care
questions.explanation: A lead container with long-handled forceps stays in the room, assignments rotate to limit each nurse's exposure, and staff wear dosimeters to track dose. A dislodged implant is picked up only with forceps, never by hand, even gloved, and pregnant visitors are not allowed at all.

questions.stem: A client who speaks only Vietnamese is having a mental health assessment through a qualified medical interpreter. Which action by the nurse is appropriate?
options: Ask the interpreter to summarize replies
Have the client's adult son interpret
Face and speak directly to the client
questions.explanation: The nurse looks at and speaks to the client in the first person, and the interpreter translates everything word for word. A summary loses the client's own words, which matter in a mental status assessment, and a family member may filter answers about mood, safety or substance use.

| Sodium | 134 mEq/L |
questions.stem: A client with bipolar disorder takes lithium 300 mg three times daily. Complete the sentence. The findings are most consistent with [[1]], and the nurse should first [[2]].
questions.explanation: A level of 2.2 mEq/L with vomiting, coarse tremor and slurred speech is lithium toxicity (maintenance range about 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L), so further doses are held and the HCP notified. Gastroenteritis can cause vomiting but not a toxic level, and adding salt does not treat toxicity already present.

questions.stem: A client who had a lumbar puncture this morning reports a headache that worsens when sitting up and eases when lying down. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Raise the head of the bed to 45 degrees
Apply a warm pack to the site
questions.explanation: A positional headache after lumbar puncture comes from CSF leaking at the puncture site, and lying flat with generous fluids relieves it while it seals. Raising the head of the bed worsens it, and restricting fluids slows CSF replacement.

questions.passage:
1400: IV running at 150 mL/hr since surgery. Intake exceeds output by 3,200 mL over 24 hours.
1415: Crackles in both lungs, neck veins distended at 45 degrees. SpO2 89%, RR 26.
questions.stem: The nurse reviews notes on a 78-year-old client receiving IV fluids after surgery. Which problem do the findings best support?
questions.explanation: Bilateral crackles, distended neck veins and a large positive fluid balance in an older adult on continuous IV fluids point to fluid overload. Pneumonia would not explain the neck vein distention or the fluid balance.

questions.stem: A pediatric nurse floats to an adult medical unit. Which client is most appropriate for the charge nurse to assign to this nurse?
options: Client on a continuous insulin infusion for DKA
Client just returned from cardiac catheterization
Client with stable asthma on scheduled inhalers
Client with a new tracheostomy and copious secretions
questions.explanation: A float nurse should receive a stable client whose care matches skills the nurse already has, such as asthma management. A fresh tracheostomy, an insulin infusion for DKA and a client just back from catheterization are less stable and need closer, unit-specific monitoring.

questions.stem: The parent of a 2-year-old says the child has a tantrum every morning over choosing clothes. Which guidance should the nurse give?
options: Let the child choose any outfit freely
Offer two outfits to choose from
questions.explanation: Toddlers are working on autonomy, and a limited choice between two acceptable options supports independence while keeping limits. Unlimited choice overwhelms a toddler and can lead to unsafe or unsuitable picks, and removing choice increases power struggles.

questions.stem: A client is on prolonged bed rest. Which interventions help prevent complications of immobility? Select all that apply.
options: Massage the calves to aid flow
questions.explanation: Deep breathing prevents atelectasis, range of motion prevents contractures, and compression devices reduce venous stasis. Calf massage can dislodge a clot, and fluid restriction raises the risk of urinary stasis, constipation and thrombosis.

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia has taken clozapine for 3 months. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Hold the dose and notify the HCP
Give the dose, recheck ANC weekly
Give half the usual dose today
questions.explanation: An ANC of 900/mcL is moderate neutropenia (500 to 999), and with sore throat and fever it may signal infection, so clozapine is interrupted and the HCP notified; ANC monitoring still applies after the REMS ended. Giving any dose, even a reduced one, continues the drug causing the neutropenia.

questions.stem: A nurse prepares a medication for the wrong client but notices the error while checking the wristband and does not give it. How is this event classified?
questions.explanation: A near miss is an error caught before it reaches the client, and reporting it helps find the system cause. Adverse, sentinel and never events are errors or events that actually reached a client.

questions.stem: The HCP orders a medication dose that is twice the usual maximum dose. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Ask pharmacy to send a lower dose
Clarify the order with the HCP
Give the dose as it is written
Give half the dose and document why
questions.explanation: The nurse is accountable for every dose given, so an order outside the safe range is clarified with the prescriber before giving anything. Changing the dose or asking pharmacy to substitute is practicing outside the nurse's authority.
